HD.rationale: Home Depot presents a deteriorating fundamental picture with accelerating margin compression, extreme balance-sheet leverage, and a valuation that offers zero equity risk premium over Treasuries. The stock is cheaper than it was, but it is cheaper because earnings are declining — not because the market has mispriced stable earnings power. Without evidence of margin stabilization or a clear earnings inflection, the quantitative case for fundamental attractiveness is weak. The strong OCF is the best counterargument, but it must be weighed against the structural leverage risk in a rising-rate environment.
key_factors: EPS diluted fell to $3.30 from $3.45 YoY (-4.3%) and from $3.62 QoQ (-8.8%) — revenue growth not translating to earnings
Gross margin compressed to 33.0% from 33.8% YoY; operating margin dropped to 11.9% from 12.9% — accelerating margin erosion
Operating cash flow surged to $6.03B (+39.5% YoY) — strongest fundamental element, but insufficient to offset leverage risk
Total liabilities of $94.03B against equity of $13.87B yields D/E of 6.78x — extreme leverage leaves minimal room for earnings downturn
PE diluted of 23.7x sits below 365-day midpoint of 24.6x but earnings yield of 4.2% is below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.68% — zero equity risk premium
DIY customer retrenching on big-ticket projects amid housing affordability pressure; management stated 'larger discretionary projects remain under pressure'
Tariff headwinds (10-12.5% across 86 countries) increase cost exposure for HD's imported merchandise assortment
Q2 earnings due August 18 with consensus EPS of $4.71, marginally above $4.68 year-ago — little room for disappointment
Organizational realignment (2026-07-30) created Office of Pro Acceleration — proactive but unproven near-term catalyst
WTI crude oil fell from ~$110 to ~$85 (-22%) — potential logistics/input cost relief with a lag
